finding: A ready command that runs out of timeout_minutes in premerge-check leaves its child processes running. run_ready_commands starts the command with subprocess.run(shell=True, timeout=...). On the time-out, Python kills only the shell, so every process that the ready script started keeps running after premerge-check has exited 3. A scratch check with a ready script that starts `sleep 30` twice showed both sleeps alive after the TimeoutExpired. crap-score stops the process group of a timed-out command, SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after 5 seconds (crap-score, section Stops), so the two runners of one ready command behave differently. The time limit itself is not in BR-136, and the second row of spec-feedback-ST-0443.md reports that. The behavior looks unintended. Fix: in premerge-check, start the ready command in its own session and stop its process group on the time-out, as run_command of crap-score does, and add a test with a ready stub that sleeps past a short timeout_minutes.
why_this_severity: The code exists only on the story branch, so it is not in use. BR-136 sets no time limit for a ready command, so the merge still stops with exit 3 as required (no to fails_purpose). After a time-out, the User must find and stop the leftover processes of a half-started stack by hand before resume-gates, because those processes can keep a port or a container of the shared service busy for the next run.
